actions.reason: C0001 has a coherent RNA-defined metabolic downregulation program with large effect sizes and FDR significance. WXS and CNV are not significant but do not actively contradict the identity. Per-set technical associations are not significant, and structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining C0001 as a discovery-stage candidate is better supported than Drop.

C0002 has moderate cross-modal support: RNA shows FDR-significant pathway changes, CNV shows FDR-significant copy-number losses, and WSI/RNA provide positive silhouette support. Per-set technical associations are not significant. Structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. The candidate identity is sufficiently defensible for downstream validation.

C0003 lacks coherent biological identity: only one RNA pathway is FDR-significant, WXS and CNV show no significant findings, and cross-modal consistency is weak with only CT positive. The evidence is broadly weak and inconsistent, and no structural correction or resolvable evidence request is preferable. Dropping is better supported than retaining.

C0004 has no significant biological findings in any modality after FDR correction, and cross-modal consistency is weak with high PAC indicating instability. The absence of positive identity evidence, combined with lack of structural support for Split or Merge, makes retention indefensible. Dropping is better supported than Accept.

C0005 is strongly confounded by technical factors: per-set tests show significant associations with CT manufacturer, scanner model, and reconstruction kernel, and the set is primarily CT-driven with high CT silhouette. The biological evidence is absent (no significant findings in any modality). The measured technical explanation plausibly dominates the identity, so dropping is better supported than retaining.

C0006 has strong biological support: RNA shows FDR-significant inflammatory/interferon upregulation with large effect sizes, and WXS shows significant BAP1 enrichment. Cross-modal consistency is moderate with WSI and RNA positive and highest patient support. Per-set technical associations are not significant. Structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining C0006 is better supported than Drop.
